findings.statement: keccak_final writes the context's md_size bytes to `out` whenever outlen > 0 (src/provider/digest.rs:1394-1396) and never requires md_size <= outlen. EVP_DigestFinalXOF (src/evp/digest.rs:2779) passes the caller's `size` as outlen and calls dfinal on `set_params >= 0`, which is 0 for a fixed SHA3 row, so EVP_DigestFinalXOF(sha3_256, buf16, 16) writes 32 bytes. 3.6.4 has the same shape (sha3_prov.c:112-129, digest.c:530): conserved, not introduced, but the crate's own # Safety at :2726 admits the call. Control B2-KFINAL.

EVP_DigestFinal_ex (:2646) and EVP_DigestFinalXOF (:2779) call dfinal with (*ctx).algctx and no NULL test. A refused NEWCTX (:2328-2332) leaves digest set and algctx NULL, so EVP_DigestFinal_ex on that context calls a final with NULL; sha1::internal_final (:692), md5_sha1::internal_final (:1199) and keccak_final (:1388) then dereference it. blake2 is protected because it publishes GETTABLE_CTX_PARAMS and get_ctx_params refuses NULL (:1952). Control B2-FINALNULL. This is the batch-1 F1 state with a second sink.

16 of the 19 records carry coordinate_check.actual_definition_line = 433/465/479/515/596, which are the `digest_impl!`/`sha1::set_ctx_params` items, while the recorded site is a different, hand-written function (dupctx 647/959/1154/1337/1885, get_params 705/1019/1214/2039, internal_final 682/1189/2013, internal_init 670/1177/1975, set_ctx_params 1912). `stale` is still reported false, so the field that says which definition was bound is name-resolved, not identity-resolved (§22). Only 026/018/020 are correct. The recorded line and span hash are correct in all 19: B2-SPAN 19/19, B2-ITEM 19/19.

None of the 19 definitions carries a `# Safety` section; the receipt nonetheless records criteria.contract = PASS for all of them. The contract text lives only in the receipt and in `// SAFETY:` block comments. (The functions are private, so clippy's missing_safety_doc does not fire — which is why this was not caught mechanically.)

All 19 obligations carry the SAME 112-element boundary_ids list, so the inventory->receipt join is non-discriminating; the discharging row is named only by discharge_boundary_id. This is the batch-1 'boundary row accepted by a content address' class in its inventory form. Control B2-JOIN.

The batch-1 NULL-algctx copyctx defect is unchanged on this candidate: copyctx((*out).algctx, (*in_).algctx) at src/evp/digest.rs:3042 and :3079 still has no algctx test. B2-COPYCTX FAIL is the recurrence witness (K10 flips it).

All 19 rows cite the same generic `established_by` sentence ('caller: src/evp/digest.rs and the provider dispatch … obtain the algctx from NEWCTX/DUPCTX') with no coordinate, so §22's per-call-site witness is absent everywhere. For the four `get_params` rows (006/009/015/030) the sentence is not merely generic but inapplicable: that ABI slot (OSSL_FUNC_digest_get_params, called at src/evp/digest.rs:1168) has no algctx parameter at all.

Boundary OSSH-V1I-026's contract says the function 'returns 1'; the body returns 0 when OSSL_PARAM_set_uint refuses the located entry (:1967). No write occurs on that path, so this is a contract inaccuracy, not a safety gap.

blake2::internal_final returns 0 for `outsz < outlen` without raising PROV_R_INVALID_DIGEST_SIZE, which the authority raises at blake2_prov.c:238 (ERROR_PASS). Observed in source; no error-queue court was run here.
